title: Zaporozhian Cossacks
capsule: The Zaporozhian Cossacks were a semi-autonomous Cossack host centered below the Dnieper rapids (za porohamy, 'beyond the rapids') in what is now southern Ukraine, governed from the Sich fortified headquarters. After the Pereiaslav Agreement of 1654 bound them to Muscovy, the host retained considerable autonomy and became a flashpoint in rivalry among Russia, Poland-Lithuania, and the Ottoman Empire during the Ruin (1657–1687). Hetman Ivan Mazepa's alliance with Sweden's Charles XII ended at Poltava in 1709, when Peter I destroyed the Sich and expelled the host briefly; it was reconstituted under Russian supervision as the New Sich in 1734 but finally abolished by Catherine II's decree in 1775 to clear the way for colonial settlement of Novorossiya.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Sich locations are archaeologically and cartographically documented; the host's territorial claims over the steppe frontier are approximate and contested in historiography.
